'''Matagalpa''' is an extinct [[Misumalpan]] language formerly spoken in the central highlands of [[Nicaragua]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Campbell |first=Lyle |title=The Languages of Native America |chapter-url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.7560/746244-018/html |chapter=Middle American Languages |date=2021-10-25 |pages=902–1000 |publisher=University of Texas Press |isbn=978-0-292-76851-2 |language=en |doi=10.7560/746244-018}}</ref>

It was closely related to [[Cacaopera language|Cacaopera]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Wierzbicka |first=Anna |date=1994 |title=Semantic and Lexical Universals |url=https://www.torrossa.com/en/resources/an/5063254?digital=true |journal=Semantic and Lexical Universals |language=en |pages=1–520}}</ref> The ethnic group, which numbers about 20,000, now speaks [[Spanish language|Spanish]].

According to local inhabitants familiar with remote regions, the language may still be spoken in the highland areas of Azancor, Musún, and Pancasan, located in [[Matagalpa Department]]. Many words of Matagalpa are still used in the region.<ref>{{cite web |title=Vestiges of Ancient Indigenous Language Still Found Today in Matagalpa's Northern Highlands |url=https://ticotimes.net/2008/01/11/vestiges-of-ancient-indigenous-language-still-found-today-in-matagalpa-s-northern-highlands |website=The Tico Times |access-date=14 April 2025 |date=11 January 2008}}</ref>
